tips.title: Airbrushing: Achieving Smooth Transitions with a Gradation Mask
tips.text: Use a thin, flexible film of transparent tape to create a gradation mask for airbrushing. Apply the tape at a 45-degree angle to create a smooth transition between two colors. Use a high-quality airbrush with a 0.5mm nozzle and a suitable air pressure setting to maintain a consistent flow of paint.

tips.title: Hand Painting: Creating Realistic Metallic Effects with Alkyd Paint
tips.text: Mix alkyd paint with a high-solidity resin (e.g., Vallejo's Alkyd Thinner) to create a durable, glossy finish. Apply multiple thin layers, allowing each layer to dry before adding the next. Use a brush with synthetic fibers to achieve a smooth, even finish. For realistic metallic effects, add a small amount of metallic powder (e.g., aluminum or copper) to the paint mixture.

tips.title: Primer: Using a Texture Spray for Enhanced Detail
tips.text: Use a texture spray (e.g., Tamiya's Fine Surface Primer) to create a raised, textured surface for detailing. Apply the primer with a brush, allowing it to dry completely before adding paint or washes. This technique is particularly effective for creating realistic stone or concrete surfaces.

tips.title: Decals: Applying Thin, Flexible Decals with a Water-Based Adhesive
tips.text: Use a water-based decal adhesive (e.g., Microscale's Set & Peel) to apply decals to curved or irregular surfaces. Apply a thin layer of adhesive to the decal, then position it on the model. Use a small brush to smooth out any air bubbles or wrinkles.

tips.title: Weathering: Using a Combination of Washes and Dry Brushing for Realistic Effects
tips.text: Combine a dark wash (e.g., Citadel's Nuln Oil) with dry brushing to create realistic, multi-layered weathering effects. Apply the wash to recessed areas, then use a dry brush to pick out raised details. Repeat the process with lighter washes and brushstrokes to achieve a natural, weathered appearance.
